title: 10-12. THE SEARCH BEGINS WITH THE OLDEST

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Very well, then,' he said, 'let it be as you say. Whoever is found to have it will become my slave; the rest of you will be free from blame.' Each of them quickly lowered his sack to the ground and opened it. Then the steward proceeded to search, beginning with the oldest and ending with the youngest. And the cup was found in Benjamin's sack." — Gen 44:10-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Picture the scene. The steward starts with Reuben, the eldest. Nothing. Simeon. Nothing. One by one down the line, and each time the brothers must have felt a little more relieved, a little more vindicated. See? We told you. Nine sacks opened and nothing found.

Then the last sack. Benjamin's.

The search is deliberately slow, and Joseph designed it that way. Each empty sack raises their confidence higher, so that the discovery lands with maximum force. This is not cruelty; it is the careful work of a man determined to get to the bottom of his brothers' hearts.

There is a lesson here about how God deals with us. He is not in a hurry. He often works slowly, opening one sack at a time, until the real issue is finally exposed. We would prefer quick answers and fast resolutions. God prefers thorough work.

And when the truth finally comes out, it lands hardest on the one person nobody expected. The brothers' world collapses in a single moment — but that collapse is the beginning of the healing this family has waited twenty years for. God's most painful moments in our lives are often the doorway to His deepest restorations.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Why do you think God often works slowly rather than quickly in our lives?
2. Has God ever exposed something in your life at a moment you least expected?
3. Can you think of a painful moment that God later used to restore something broken?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are never in a hurry and never careless. Give me patience with Your slow, thorough work in me, and trust that even painful exposure is the road to healing. Amen.
